title: Marlar, Greg B, Claim Disposition Agreement Order
text:
70 Van Natta 171 (2018) 171
In the Matter of the Compensation of
GREG B. MARLAR, Claimant
WCB Case No: 17-03005C
ORDER DENYING RECONSDIERATION OF CLAIM DISPOSITION
AGREEMENT
Bennett Hartman Morris & Kaplan, Claimant Attorneys
Cummins Goodman et al, Defense Attorneys
Reviewing Panel: Members Lanning and Johnson.
On December 19, 2017, we approved the parties’ Claim Disposition
Agreement (CDA) in the above-captioned matter. Pursuant to that agreement, in
consideration of the payment of a stated sum, claimant released certain rights to
future workers’ compensation benefits, except medical services-related benefits,
for his compensable injury.
On January 29, 2018, we received an “addendum” to the CDA. We treat the
submission as a motion for reconsideration of the approved CDA. The request is
denied.
An order approving the disposition of a claim is not subject to review.
ORS 656.236(2). However, the Board may reconsider final orders under
ORS 656.236, provided that the motion is filed within 10 days of the mailing
of the order. OAR 438-009-0035(1), (2).
Here, the CDA was approved on December 19, 2017. See OAR 438-009-
0028(1); OAR 438-009-0030(6). The parties’ addendum to the CDA was filed on
January 29, 2018. Because the motion was untimely filed, it cannot be considered.
See Mark J. Lackey, 63 Van Natta 795 (2011); Randy G. Shamblin, 62 Van
Natta 40 (2010); Carl E. Worley, 47 Van Natta 1636 (1995) (denying
reconsideration of a previous CDA approval where an amendment regarding
“Social Security offsets” was submitted after the 10-day reconsideration period had
lapsed); cf. Vincent Rhea, 69 Van Natta 1333 (2017) (the parties’ second CDA for
the same claim was approved where the second agreement included “Social
Security-related” language, but also was supported by separate consideration for
further release of the claimant’s rights).
Consequently, based on the aforementioned reasoning, we lack authority to
alter the previously approved CDA. Accordingly, the motion for reconsideration is
denied.
IT IS SO ORDERED.
Entered at Salem, Oregon on February 6, 2018
